name: San Francisco Proposition I (November 1994)
effective: From the date of certification of the measure for covered units (certification date not stated in the text)

components.cap_unit: share of the rise in the regional consumer price index (allowable annual increase for sitting tenants)
source_sentences: Rental units in owner-occupied buildings of two to four units built before June 1979 become subject to the Rent Ordinance.
For a covered unit, the landlord may raise the rent of a sitting tenant once a year by no more than the allowable increase, which is 60 percent of the rise in the regional consumer price index.
When a tenant leaves voluntarily, the landlord may set the rent for the next tenant freely, after which the limit applies again.
The Rent Board hears tenant petitions and landlord applications and may order rent reductions and refunds.
Rental units in owner-occupied buildings of two to four units built before June 1979 become subject to the Rent Ordinance.
Tenants of covered units may be evicted only for one of the just causes listed in the Rent Ordinance.

unclear.text: When a tenant leaves voluntarily, the landlord may set the rent for the next tenant freely, after which the limit applies again.
readings: U1-a: the free reset of rent applies only when the tenant leaves voluntarily; a departure forced by eviction or other involuntary means does not free the rent
U1-b: 'voluntarily' is not defined in the text, so a departure induced by landlord pressure or a buyout may count as voluntary and free the rent

reading_facts.U1-a: no rent reset after involuntary departure

unclear.text: Rental units in owner-occupied buildings of two to four units built before June 1979 become subject to the Rent Ordinance.
readings: U2-a: owner occupancy is tested at enactment; buildings the owner occupied in 1994 are covered, and a building later vacated by the owner is covered only under the existing ordinance
U2-b: owner occupancy is a continuing condition of the exemption; the change removes the exemption for these buildings whatever the owner's later residence

reading_facts.U2-a: coverage fixed at enactment for owner-occupied buildings
reading_facts.U2-b: coverage follows the owner's current residence

unclear.text: For a covered unit, the landlord may raise the rent of a sitting tenant once a year by no more than the allowable increase, which is 60 percent of the rise in the regional consumer price index.
readings: U3-a: the regional CPI rise is measured over the most recent twelve months before the increase
U3-b: the regional CPI rise is measured since the tenant's previous increase

context: Before Proposition I, annual rent increases for sitting tenants were limited in most rental buildings built before June 1979, under the Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance in force since 1979. Source: "Since 1979 the San Francisco Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance has limited annual rent increases for sitting tenants in most rental buildings built before June 1979."
Before Proposition I, buildings of four units or fewer in which the owner lived were exempt from that limit. Source: "Buildings of four units or fewer in which the owner lives were exempt."
